name: What type of drywall should be installed in a garage?

mainEntity.name: What type of drywall should be installed in a garage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall type depends on code fire-separation requirements and how you plan to use the space. Shared walls between an attached garage and the home typically require 5/8-inch Type X fire-rated drywall to provide a mandated fire barrier. For exterior walls and ceilings, 1/2-inch drywall is common, though 5/8-inch is often preferred on garage ceilings to avoid sagging between wider truss spacing. In moisture-prone garage areas, mold- and moisture-resistant panels may be considered. A general contractor inspects your garage framing layout to specify the correct board thickness before hanging begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached garage walls sharing space with living quarters generally require 5/8-inch Type X fire-rated drywall, while 1/2-inch or 5/8-inch boards are standard for other walls and ceilings.
